essay: School uniforms should be required in secondary schools. First, uniforms reduce the pressure to wear expensive brands. Requiring uniforms is a simple answer to a complicated problem. Supporters claim that uniforms end bullying, yet students quickly find other markers of status, such as shoes, phones and bags. Uniforms also carry a real cost: a full set can cost more than ordinary clothes, and families must replace it as children grow. A better policy is a basic dress code that sets limits on offensive or unsafe clothing while leaving choice to students. This keeps the benefit of a calm school environment without forcing every family to buy special clothing. Schools should therefore drop compulsory uniforms in favour of a clear dress code.

Uniforms help students feel part of a community. When I visited a school with uniforms, the students seemed proud of their school and behaved well on trips, because people could see which school they were from. Uniforms also make it easier for teachers to spot visitors who do not belong in the building. On the other hand, they can be uncomfortable in summer. Schools could solve this with a lighter summer uniform. Overall I believe the benefits are bigger than the problems.

Making uniforms required would save families money in the long run. Instead of buying many fashionable outfits, parents can buy three or four sets of the uniform and reuse them. Many schools also run second-hand uniform sales, which lowers the cost even more. In addition, uniforms remove a daily source of arguments at home about what is acceptable to wear. Critics say uniforms are old-fashioned, but practical solutions do not need to be fashionable. For these reasons uniforms should be required.

Uniforms should not be required because they do not improve learning. Studies on uniforms and test scores show mixed results, and some find no difference at all. If the goal of school is learning, money and time should go to teachers and materials, not to clothing rules. Enforcing a uniform also takes up staff time, for example when students are sent home for wearing the wrong jacket. That time would be better spent teaching.

essay: Mobile phones should be banned during lessons. Phones are designed to grab attention with notifications, and even a phone lying on the desk can distract a student. Some argue that phones are useful for research, but schools can provide laptops or tablets that are only used for school work. Therefore a classroom ban on personal phones is the best choice.

Homework is necessary because practice is how skills become permanent. In class there is only time to explain a new idea and do a few examples. At home, students can practise on their own and discover what they have not understood yet. This shows the teacher where help is needed. Homework also teaches planning and responsibility, which are important for university and work. However, homework should be short and meaningful, not busy work. With that condition, homework clearly supports learning.

Whether homework is necessary depends on its purpose. Homework that repeats what was done in class adds little, but homework that asks students to apply an idea in a new situation can deepen understanding. Research suggests that for older students a moderate amount of homework is linked to better results, while for young children the effect is small. Schools should therefore keep homework for older students, limit the time it takes, and design tasks that require thinking rather than copying. In this form, homework is a useful part of learning.

I believe homework is necessary, especially for subjects like mathematics and languages. Learning vocabulary or practising equations needs repetition, and there is simply not enough time in class for that. When I stopped doing my English homework for a month, my test results went down. Homework also prepares students for exams, where they have to work alone. It should not be too long, though, because tired students do not learn well.

Homework should be optional. Students who want extra practice can choose to do it, and students who already understand the topic can use their time for other things. Making homework optional also shows students that they are responsible for their own learning. Teachers can still offer practice tasks and feedback for those who hand them in. This approach respects that students learn in different ways.

Homework is necessary but the current amount is too high. A good rule would be about ten minutes per grade level, so a student in grade ten would have around one hundred minutes per day at most. More than that leads to stress without improving results. Teachers of different subjects should also coordinate, so that big assignments are not all due in the same week. With these limits, homework can keep its benefits without harming students' wellbeing.
